newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Conservation Reserve Program signup brisk.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Conservation Reserve Program signup brisk.

text.p: Early signup activity in the government's new Conservation Reserve Program has been brisk, said an Agriculture Department official on Wednesday.

While not releasing any specific numbers on the total amount of acres that have been offered to the program since March 3 when signup began, the official said that the states with the biggest amount of acres already enrolled in the CRP are reporting the most activity.
"Things are going real well. Interest is very high," said USDA spokesman Jim Petterson. "There's been a lot of early sign-up activity."

Producers have until the end of the month to offer land into the government's new 10-year program. USDA has pledged it would notify farmers by mid-June on whether or not their land has been accepted into the program.
Petterson said that so far enrollment seems to be most active in states with already big CRP enrollment -- Texas, the Dakotas, Kansas, Montana, Nebraska, Minnesota, Iowa, Missouri.
"Places where there already are a lot of people in the CRP, that's where activity has been highest," said Petterson.

The Agriculture Department last month announced a sweeping new CRP with new eligibility criteria. The new criteria would in effect make two-thirds of the nation's cropland eligible for the program. The department wants to maintain about 36 million acres of the most fragile land in the program.
Petterson said USDA staff has been keeping up with the activity, and that the process has so far been very smooth.
